## Principles

Generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Cursor, etc.) can help you **learn**.  
They must not replace your own understanding on **graded work**.

**Bottom line:** submitted notebooks, assignments, checkpoint practicals, and presentations must be work you can explain and defend.

Unauthorized use is treated as **academic misconduct** under University of Bern rules.

---

## How you **can** use AI (learning)

Allowed for study and exploration, for example:

- Clarifying concepts from lectures (Lotka–Volterra, establishment, rescue, …)
- Asking for an alternative explanation of a step you already tried
- Generating **practice** questions (not solutions to graded tasks)
- Brainstorming project / model ideas — if **you** implement and justify the final version
- Help interpreting an error message **after** you have attempted a fix

If AI helped you learn, you should still be able to redo the key steps without it.

---

## How you **cannot** use AI (graded work)

Not allowed:

- Submitting AI-generated answers, text, or code as your own for homework, notebooks, checkpoint products, or slides
- Having AI write your model, analysis, or presentation and turning it in with only light edits
- Copy-pasting AI prose into reflections, captions, or talk scripts
- Using AI during any closed / proctored assessment (if we hold one)
- Using AI to fabricate citations, data, or lab claims

**Presentations (Checkpoints A–D):** you must be able to explain every figure and modelling choice live. If you cannot, that is evidence the work is not yours.

---

## Mandatory disclosure

If you used AI at all while preparing a **graded** submission (including debugging help or brainstorming), add an **AI disclosure** at the end:

```text
AI disclosure
- Tool: …
- How used: … (be specific: which function / which paragraph)
- I confirm the final submission reflects my own understanding and I can explain it.
```

No AI used → write: `AI disclosure: none`.

Missing or false disclosure can itself be treated as misconduct.

---

## Course-specific expectations

| Activity | AI stance |
|---|---|
| Weekly notebooks (formative) | Learning help OK; disclosure if used on anything you submit |
| Checkpoint practicals (A–D) | Your code + figures; disclosure required if AI was involved |
| Checkpoint presentations | Your words; AI is not a co-presenter |
| Week 14 portfolio wrap | Same as checkpoints |

We may ask follow-up questions about your code, figures, or biological interpretation.

---

## Why this policy exists

This course trains **quantitative biological judgement**: turning biology into updates, reading real data, and communicating limits.

Those skills only stick if **you** struggle productively with the material. AI can be a tutor; it cannot be your substitute teammate on graded work.

---

## Questions

If unsure whether a use is allowed, ask **before** submitting — in class or by email.
